concept.name: Weekly loss limit
concept.definition: A risk control that suspends or down-sizes trading for the remainder of the week once cumulative weekly losses reach a preset threshold, layering a slower-timescale brake on top of daily loss limits.
concept.intuition: Bad weeks cluster when a system is out of sync with the regime; the weekly cap forces a pause and review before a rough patch becomes a ruined month.
concept.mechanics: Aggregate realized (and, in strict implementations, unrealized) P/L from the week's reference equity; on breach, flatten and/or halt trading until the next week or cut size by a fixed factor such as 50%. Practitioner conventions commonly run about 3-6% of weekly starting equity.
concept.formula: Breach if equity_t < reference_equity_week - L_weekly, with L_weekly the weekly allowance (e.g. 5% of weekly starting equity).
concept.failure_modes: Like any path-based cap it can be jumped by gaps and is arbitrary relative to the strategy's actual loss distribution; rigid weekly stops can also lock in losses at the worst point of a mean-reverting stretch.
concept.misconceptions: A weekly limit is not a substitute for per-trade risk control — a single oversized trade can consume it in minutes — and hitting it repeatedly signals a system problem, not merely bad luck.
concept.example: A trader with a 5% weekly limit on $100,000 who loses $5,000 by Thursday stops trading until Monday, when the limit resets against the new reference equity.

citations.source: Trade Loss Tracker: extended summary of Van K. Tharp, The Definitive Guide to Position Sizing Strategies
citations.section: Framework 3: Intraday Risk Budget Allocation (weekly loss limit layer)
